【随机选分支】请掷一枚六面骰子,点数几就选分支几(1→分支1 … 6→分支6)。也可用手机秒数个位:1-6对应分支;若为0/7/8/9请再掷/再看一次直到1-6。勿按个人喜好挑选。
Roll a six-sided die: face N → Branch N. Or use seconds digit 1-6 (retry if 0/7/8/9). Do not choose by preference.

【分支1】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题。
[Branch 1] Read the sonnet, then answer the next three items.
The orchard yields its last and blunted gold,
And branches, stripped, hold nothing to the sky.
The gathered wind grows sharp, and over-bold,
To teach the lingering leaves the art to fly.
I watch the laden wagon creak and strain
Through ruts of mud, toward the granary door,
While in my hand a single grain of grain
Remembers all the summer’s heavy store.
The light withdraws, a curtain drawn on glass,
And every shadow stretches long and thin,
As if the day, too, knew it could not pass
Unnoticed, and would leave its marks on skin.
So let the season’s turning have its way;
I keep the quiet ache of this last day.

【分支2】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题。
[Branch 2] Read the sonnet, then answer the next three items.
The maple thrusts its scarlet lance on high,
And wrestles with the wind’s insistent pull,
Whose cold breath strips the gold leaf from the sky
To scatter coins across the river’s hull.
The orchard boughs, once heavy, now unload
Their burden to the furrow’s patient bed,
Where wasps in drunken circles stab and goad
The bruises of the fruit that they have fed.
But see—the swallow’s keel cuts through the gray,
A final stitch that binds the fading hem,
Then snaps the thread and tears the light away,
And leaves the naked scaffolding to stem
The long descent—till winter’s hammer knocks
The last bright season flat against the rocks.

【分支3】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题。
[Branch 3] Read the sonnet, then answer the next three items.
The city’s pulse is muffled by the rain,
A silver hush that slicks the iron rails.
My window holds the ghost of a lit train,
Whose fading roar through dripping glass prevails.
The asphalt breathes a spectrum of dull gold,
And gutters choke with the confetti of the hours.
I trace a cold mouth on the pane—a fold
Of fog, a whispered script the lamplight scours.
The clock across the square is stopped at one,
A blind man’s face that cannot see the chill.
The cables overhead, a slackened gun,
Sag with the weight of voices gone to still.
So let the dark unspool its thread of gray;
I wear this solitude like a frayed coat today.

【分支4】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题。
[Branch 4] Read the sonnet, then answer the next three items.
The city’s iron ribs exhale a breath
Of diesel fumes and rain-washed asphalt gray.
A single lamp-post stitches light from death,
And tracks my shadow’s slow and stolen way.
The pavement drinks the echo of my tread,
A hollow drumbeat on a stage of stone.
The windows, shutters drawn like lids of lead,
Keep vigil for the sleep they must atone.
But here the silence sharpens to a blade—
It slices through the murmur of the wire,
And every distant siren, unafraid,
Becomes a ghost that walks through my desire.
Then, sudden, from the gutter’s choked-up throat,
A star—unbroken—floats upon the moat.

【分支5】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题。
[Branch 5] Read the sonnet, then answer the next three items.
The ledger of the lake keeps every stone
That ever sank, in silted, patient rows;
The current’s cursive, cursive and alone,
Erases what the surface can’t disclose.
I plunge my hand to sift the muddy cold,
And bring up shards of a forgotten noon—
A sunken coin, a story briefly told,
That darkens as it dries beneath the moon.
The water’s weight is memory’s own press,
A slow compaction of the vanished days,
And what I lift is only loneliness,
A cold, unpolished pebble’s muted grays.
So let the deep keep what the deep has kept;
I’ll turn and leave the ripples, unaccept.

【分支6】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题。
[Branch 6] Read the sonnet, then answer the next three items.
The river keeps what daylight cannot hold,
a sunken coin, a leaf, a rusted key;
its current turns the story green and cold,
and every ripple drags a thought from me.
I wade through half-remembered autumns, deep
where silt has softed the edges of a name;
my fingers sift the shallows, try to keep
a fragment that the water bends to flame.
But night descends, and all the river swells—
it lunges at the bank with sudden tooth,
and what I thought was mine, the current quells,
a drowning echo severed from its truth.
So let it take the wreckage of my years;
I'll drink the dark and call the flood my tears.
